tool.name: RSEM calculate expression
tool.command: mkdir reference && rsem-prepare-reference #if str($reference.source) == 'genome': --gtf '$reference.gtf' #elif $reference.transcript_to_gene_map: --transcript-to-gene-map '$reference.transcript_to_gene_map' #end if '$reference.fasta' reference/rsem > rsem.log && rsem-sam-validator '$alignments' > validation.log && cat validation.log >> rsem.log && ## RSEM 1.3.3's validator also returns zero for invalid input. if ! grep -qFx 'The input file is valid!' validation.log; then cat validation.log >&2; exit 1; fi && rsem-calculate-expression --alignments --num-threads \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if str($library.layout) == 'paired': --paired-end #else: --fragment-length-mean $library.fragment_length_mean --fragment-length-sd $library.fragment_length_sd #end if --strandedness '$strandedness' --seed-length $advanced.seed_length $advanced.estimate_rspd $advanced.append_names #if str($output_bam) == 'false': --no-bam-output #end if '$alignments' reference/rsem rsem_out >> rsem.log

param.label: Transcriptome alignments
param.help: Use transcript coordinates, for example STAR's Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam. Alignments for each read must be grouped together, with paired mates adjacent. Genomic alignments are unsuitable.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Reference genome
param.help: Use the same genome assembly that was used for alignment.

param.label: Gene annotation
param.help: Use the same annotation and transcript identifiers that were used to produce the transcriptome alignments.

param.name: fasta
param.label: Reference transcripts
param.help: Sequence identifiers, lengths, and sequences must match the alignment reference.

param.label: Transcript-to-gene map
param.help: Two whitespace-separated columns without a header: gene ID, then transcript ID. Without a map, each transcript is treated as a separate gene.

param.label: Mean fragment length
param.help: For single-end data, provide the mean fragment length in bases when known. The default of -1 disables the fragment-length distribution.

param.label: Fragment-length standard deviation
param.help: Provide the standard deviation in bases. A value of 0 assumes a fixed fragment length when a mean is specified.

param.label: Library strandedness
param.help: For paired-end libraries, orientation refers to the first mate relative to the transcript. Illumina TruSeq Stranded libraries normally use reverse.

param.label: Minimum read length
param.help: Reads shorter than this value are ignored. For paired-end reads, both mates must meet the threshold.

param.label: Estimate the read start position distribution
param.help: The default assumes a uniform distribution of read start positions.

param.label: Append gene and transcript names to identifiers
param.help: Names are appended when present in the GTF annotation.

param.name: output_bam
param.label: Output posterior-weighted transcriptome BAM
param.help: Includes alignments annotated with posterior probabilities. This output remains unsorted and uses transcript coordinates.

tool.help:
RSEM estimates RNA abundance for individual transcripts and their genes. A gene can produce several transcript isoforms through alternative splicing. Because a sequencing read may match a region shared by several isoforms, RSEM estimates how much each compatible transcript contributes to the observed reads. This allows ambiguous reads to contribute fractional amounts to expression estimates.
Analyze each sequencing library separately so that biological replicates remain available for subsequent comparisons. This tool starts with aligned reads and prepares the reference files needed for RSEM estimation within the job.
-----
**Transcriptome alignments**
Select the SAM or BAM dataset containing one sample's alignments to transcript sequences. These files record where each read matches a reference. With STAR, use **Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam**, produced by enabling its **TranscriptomeSAM** quantification option. A chromosome-aligned BAM uses a different coordinate system and cannot be used here.
Preserve the alternative alignments of reads that match several transcripts. RSEM uses these alternatives to estimate expression. The alignment file must retain read sequences and base-quality scores. Alignments for the same read must occur together, and the two mates of each paired-end alignment must be adjacent. The aligner must also use RSEM-compatible settings, including no insertions or deletions in alignments.
The tool checks alignment structure before estimation and stops if the check fails. An error about read grouping or mate adjacency concerns record order. RSEM's `convert-sam-for-rsem` utility can prepare the required ordering. An error about an unrecognized reference sequence instead requires checking the reference files and whether the BAM uses transcript coordinates.
-----
**Reference sequences**
This choice determines how RSEM obtains the transcript sequences and their relationships to genes.
- **Genome FASTA and GTF annotation**, the default, reconstructs transcripts from a genome sequence and its exon annotation. Choose this when you have the genome and GTF used for the preceding alignment, as in a typical STAR analysis. - **Transcript FASTA** uses sequences that already represent spliced transcripts. Choose this when your alignments were made against that transcript sequence set.
For either choice, transcript identifiers, sequences, and lengths must match the reference used to produce the alignments. Keep identifier version suffixes consistent. The same species alone is insufficient if the genome assembly or annotation release differs.
**Reference genome**
Shown with **Genome FASTA and GTF annotation**. Select the FASTA dataset containing the chromosome or contig sequences from the exact genome assembly used for alignment. The sequence names must agree with those in the GTF. For example, `chr1` and `1` are different sequence names. RSEM uses the annotated exon coordinates to extract transcript sequences from this genome.
**Gene annotation**
Shown with **Genome FASTA and GTF annotation**. Select the matching GTF dataset. Its exon records describe which genomic segments form each transcript, and its `gene_id` and `transcript_id` attributes connect transcripts to their genes. Use the same annotation release that was used to produce the transcriptome alignments. Optional `gene_name` and `transcript_name` attributes also supply the readable names used by **Append gene and transcript names to identifiers**.
**Reference transcripts**
Shown with **Transcript FASTA**. Select a FASTA dataset containing the spliced transcript sequences, with introns already removed. Each sequence identifier is treated as a transcript identifier and must match the corresponding reference name in the SAM or BAM. Use the actual transcript sequence set used for alignment, including the same identifier suffixes and sequence lengths.
**Transcript-to-gene map**
Optional and shown with **Transcript FASTA**. Supply a tab-separated dataset that assigns each transcript to a gene. It has two columns and no header. Put the **gene identifier first** and the **transcript identifier second**, despite the parameter's name. For example:
```text geneA transcriptA1 geneA transcriptA2 geneB transcriptB1 ```
Here, `transcriptA1` and `transcriptA2` contribute to the same gene-level estimate for `geneA`. Include each reference transcript once, using identifiers that match the transcript FASTA exactly.
The default is to leave this input empty. Without a map, RSEM treats each transcript as its own gene, so the gene table contains a separate entry for each transcript. Supply a map to obtain totals that combine a biological gene's isoforms. With the genome/GTF reference choice, these relationships come from the GTF automatically.
-----
**Library layout**
Choose the sequencing design of the sample:
- **Paired-end**, the default, means both ends of each library fragment were sequenced. The input alignment dataset must contain both mates. RSEM uses their positions to learn the fragment-length distribution and treats a read pair as one fragment. - **Single-end** means one end of each fragment was sequenced. This choice displays the two fragment-length settings below, because a single read does not reveal the full length of its source fragment.
Choose according to the experiment. This setting does not automatically detect or convert the library layout.
**Mean fragment length**
Shown for **Single-end** libraries. Enter the average length of the sequenced library fragments in bases, excluding sequencing adapters. A fragment is the piece of nucleic acid from which a read was generated and can extend beyond the sequenced portion. Use the fragment-size information from library preparation or another suitable measurement.
A positive value supplies the mean of a normal, or bell-shaped, fragment-length distribution. The default, **-1**, disables that fragment-length distribution. Fragment-length assumptions affect which positions in a transcript can generate a fragment and therefore influence abundance estimates, especially for short transcripts. Read length alone does not determine fragment length.
**Fragment-length standard deviation**
Shown for **Single-end** libraries. Enter the spread of fragment lengths around the mean, also in bases. A larger value represents a wider range of fragment sizes. For a library measured to have a mean of 200 bases and a standard deviation of 20 bases, enter **200** for the mean and **20** here. These values illustrate the units and must be replaced with the measurements for your library.
The default, **0**, assumes a fixed fragment length when a positive mean is supplied. This setting has no effect when the mean is **-1**, because the fragment-length distribution is disabled. Paired-end libraries learn their distribution from the paired alignments and do not use these two single-end settings.
**Library strandedness**
Stranded library preparation preserves information about which RNA strand produced a read. Choose the setting for your library preparation protocol. For paired-end data, the direction refers to **read 1**, the first mate, relative to the transcript's RNA sequence.
| Setting | Meaning | When to choose it | | --- | --- | --- | | **Unstranded** | RSEM allows reads in either orientation relative to a transcript. | The protocol does not preserve strand information. This is the default. | | **Forward** | Single-end reads, or read 1 of a pair, follow the transcript's direction. | The protocol produces reads in the same orientation as the original RNA. | | **Reverse** | Single-end reads, or read 1 of a pair, run opposite to the transcript's direction. | The protocol produces reads complementary to the original RNA. RSEM documents this setting for Illumina TruSeq Stranded libraries. |
These directions are relative to each transcript. They do not select genes on the positive or negative chromosome strand. An incorrect setting can reject compatible alignments and substantially change expression estimates. If the protocol is uncertain, recover the library-preparation information or assess strandedness before choosing. The default is an unstranded analysis and performs no automatic strand detection.
-----
**Estimation options**
These settings control read eligibility, the model of read positions, and the presentation of identifiers. For a study with several samples, use consistent analytical settings and record any changes from the defaults.
**Minimum read length**
The default is **25 bases**, and the smallest accepted value is **5 bases**. RSEM ignores reads shorter than this threshold. For paired-end data, a fragment is excluded if either mate is too short. Changing this value can therefore change which fragments contribute to expression estimates.
This option is named `--seed-length` in RSEM. In this tool, alignment has already taken place. The setting does not rerun the aligner, trim reads, or set a random-number seed. Choose it to match the read-length requirements of your analysis, especially when reproducing a published method.
**Estimate the read start position distribution**
The default is **No**, which assumes read start positions are uniformly distributed along transcripts. Select **Yes** to let RSEM estimate how the probability of observing a read varies with its start position along a transcript. This distribution is often abbreviated **RSPD**.
Library preparation can favor some transcript regions over others. Estimating this distribution lets RSEM model such positional bias when calculating abundance. It changes the statistical model and can change expression estimates. Keep the choice consistent across comparable samples or match the setting specified by the method you are reproducing.
**Append gene and transcript names to identifiers**
The default is **No**, which keeps the original gene and transcript identifiers in the result tables. Select **Yes** to append readable names from the GTF, where available, separated by an underscore. For example, a gene with `gene_id` of `g1` and `gene_name` of `GeneA` is reported as `g1_GeneA`.
This changes the labels in the result tables and leaves the abundance calculation unchanged. Readable names can help with inspection, but downstream annotation tables must use matching identifiers. Leave this option at **No** when a later analysis expects the original identifiers. A transcript FASTA and gene map alone do not supply the GTF name attributes.
-----
**Output posterior-weighted transcriptome BAM**
The default is **No**, which produces the abundance tables and log. Select **Yes** to also retain a BAM file showing RSEM's estimated probability for each alignment. A read that matches several transcripts can have several alignments with different probabilities. The probability is stored in the `ZW` tag, an additional field attached to each alignment record.
Use this output to inspect how ambiguous reads were assigned or for downstream tools that use those alignment weights. It adds a potentially large file and leaves the abundance estimates unchanged. The BAM remains unsorted and uses transcript coordinates. A viewer needs the matching transcript reference to interpret those positions.
-----
**Understanding the outputs**
- **Gene estimates** combines transcript estimates according to the GTF or supplied gene map. Without either source of gene relationships, each transcript is treated as a separate gene. - **Isoform estimates** reports expression for each transcript, including its share of its parent gene's expression in the `IsoPct` column. - **Log** records reference preparation, alignment validation, and expression estimation. Consult it when the tool fails or produces unexpected results. - **Posterior-weighted transcriptome BAM** appears only when requested, as described above.
Both abundance tables report **expected counts**, **TPM**, and **FPKM**. Expected counts estimate the number of fragments assigned to a gene or transcript. They can be fractional because ambiguous reads contribute according to their estimated probabilities. A paired-end read pair represents one fragment. Expected counts need not sum to every aligned fragment because filtering and the model's background component can exclude some contributions.
**TPM**, transcripts per million, expresses relative abundance after accounting for transcript length. **FPKM**, fragments per kilobase per million mapped fragments, is another length-normalized expression measure. **Effective length** describes the available positions from which the modeled fragments could originate. Gene-level length fields are expression-weighted averages of the corresponding transcript lengths.
-----
**Example: paired-end STAR data from a reverse-stranded library**
1. Select STAR's **Aligned.toTranscriptome.out.bam** for the sample. 2. Choose **Genome FASTA and GTF annotation**, and select the genome and annotation used for that STAR analysis. 3. Set **Library layout** to **Paired-end**. 4. Set **Library strandedness** to **Reverse**, after confirming that this matches the library protocol. 5. Use the estimation settings specified by your analysis method. Keep **Append gene and transcript names to identifiers** at **No** if downstream tools expect the original identifiers. 6. Leave **Output posterior-weighted transcriptome BAM** at **No** when only expression tables are needed.
The [RSEM expression-estimation manual](https://deweylab.github.io/RSEM/rsem-calculate-expression.html) and [reference-preparation manual](https://deweylab.github.io/RSEM/rsem-prepare-reference.html) describe the underlying model and file requirements.
